title: Toes in the Mud
checkpoint: Year 1 Autumn 2, week 1 — School readiness — Phase 5: new sounds ew, oe, au
note_for_grown_ups: A Phase 5 book for the new sound 'oe' — another way to write the /oa/ sound your child knows from 'boat', used in toe, hoe and doe.

pages.text: Ned got mud on his toes.
pages.illustration: Close on Ned's orange webbed feet completely caked in thick brown mud, seen from above. He is looking down at them, unimpressed.
Ned hopping on one foot clutching the other, beak open, having stubbed his toe on a half-buried stone. Very funny.

pages.text: Pip had a hoe in the shed.
pages.illustration: Interior of the garden shed: Pip holding up an old wooden-handled hoe far bigger than himself, presenting the solution.

pages.text: Ned did dig with the hoe.
pages.illustration: Ned dragging the hoe through the mud with both wings, leaning right back into it, cutting a deep furrow. Real effort.
A deer bounding across the far end of the garden, legs stretched, seen in silhouette through the gap in the hedge. Elegant and sudden.
The deer at full speed in the middle distance, all four feet off the ground, drawn with real grace. Both friends watching, stopped mid-action.
Close on the deer's slender feet touching the ground and leaving almost no mark, contrasted with Ned's great muddy prints beside them.
Closing page: Ned and Pip sitting on the hoe handle in the evening sun, feet clean now, the dug bed neat behind them. Satisfied.
